tasks.short: Plan retail displays, agree promotions with retailers, and assemble and replenish displays.

steps.what: Check account history, campaign brief, product availability, and display guidelines.
Inspect shelf space, stock, shopper movement, and competing displays with the retailer.
Prepare a display layout and promotional recommendation using approved examples.
Agree display placement, promotional terms, and replenishment responsibilities with the retailer.
Assemble the display, position promotional material, and replenish products.
Record display photographs, retailer commitments, and the next replenishment date.

tasks.design: A generator combines the campaign brief in {DOCS}, availability in {ERP}, and account history in {CRM} into a store visit brief and editable display templates. Configure a mobile visit form and replenishment reminders in {CRM}; the representative assesses the store, adapts the proposal, obtains retailer agreement, and builds the display.
tasks.previous_blocker: Store conditions vary, and physical execution dominates. Preparing reusable briefs and layouts was often too small a project to justify integration work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and templates handle much of the support work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting records and generating tailored packs.
tasks.still_hard: Shelf constraints, retailer preferences, physical stock handling, and attributing sales changes to a display remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Notice how the store actually works, earn retailer cooperation, and adjust the display safely on site.

ambition.what: Seasonal display refresh packs for small retailers without merchandising staff

tasks.altitude: Less time assembling visit packs leaves more time for store assessment and retailer coaching. No formal decision rights change; retailers still approve placement and promotions.

reach.task: Prepare a demonstration station that fits the agreed display.
reach.learn: Demonstration layout, shopper questions, safe product handling, and retailer operating constraints.

reach.task: Compare seasonal display trials across similar stores.
reach.learn: Baseline sales, stock availability, and simple experiment design.

evidence.claim: Templates, record retrieval, mobile forms, and reminders can support merchandising without a model.
Store assessment, retailer agreement, and physical display assembly remain predominantly human work.

assumptions: This version covers store visits where the representative also assembles and replenishes displays.
Approved campaign materials and display examples already exist.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Build ranges cover working effort; consultation waiting time may be longer.
The low automation prior fits physical execution, but preparation and recording offer separate gains.
unknowns: Whether representatives install displays or only advise retailers.
Availability of mobile access, stock records, and approved display templates.
Retailer permissions for photographs and display changes.
Whether visit records are used to monitor individual sellers.
research_questions: Which existing {CRM} configuration supports visit forms and reminders?
Which display families can use dimensional templates without losing useful local adaptation?
What employee consultation is required under national rules if visit tracking changes?
new_work: Maintain campaign templates and product mappings.
Correct stale stock information and incomplete visit records.
Check proposed layouts against current store constraints.
Maintain photograph access and retention settings.

tasks.short: Negotiate contract terms and payments, obtain exception approval, and document the agreement.

steps.what: Retrieve account history, prices, margins, payment history, and negotiating limits.
Read proposed contract changes and identify differences from approved terms.

loop.input: Customer contract draft, approved clause library, and commercial policy.
loop.output: Clause differences and potential exceptions, each linked to its source passage.
loop.check: Check clause references and quoted text; a person reviews material differences before negotiation.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per document; unresolved or unsupported clauses go to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer wording varies. Exact comparison finds edits but cannot reliably classify paraphrased obligations.

steps.what: Calculate price, volume, and payment scenarios within negotiating limits.
Discuss trade-offs and negotiate price, delivery obligations, payment dates, and other terms.
Approve commercial exceptions or return the proposal for further negotiation.
Update the contract and payment schedule to reflect approved terms.
Check the final contract against approved terms and confirm readiness for signature.
Send the approved contract for signature and record its status.

tasks.design: A deterministic calculator combines {CRM} and {ERP} records into negotiation briefs and scenarios; a bounded reader compares customer wording with the approved library in {CLM}. Configure exception routing in {WORKFLOW} and contract generation in {CLM}, then release the exact approved version through {ESIGN} after signatory approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer wording and negotiated concessions vary. Records, calculations, approval messages, and final documents often sit in separate places.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and template features cover the controlled actions. A bounded model can flag unfamiliar wording, while faster integration work connects the supporting records.
tasks.still_hard: Negotiating leverage, interpreting unusual liabilities, agreeing payment concessions, and maintaining an accurate approval mandate.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's priorities, judge concessions, and preserve trust while protecting the commercial position.

ambition.what: Evaluate payment-term alternatives during each negotiation round

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more of the week discussing trade-offs and less reconciling documents. No formal decision rights change; existing negotiating and signature mandates still apply.

reach.task: Assess requests for margin and payment-term exceptions.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, working-capital effects, approval thresholds, and precedent.

reach.task: Translate agreed terms into accurate order and billing instructions.
reach.learn: Order fields, payment schedules, delivery conditions, and contract version control.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad provides configuration and quoting linked to commercial systems; this supports controlled pricing preparation.
Deterministic scenario calculations and approved-clause templates can automate preparation without automating negotiation.
A bounded clause reader can assist review, but its classifications require validation and legal escalation.

assumptions: Negotiations concern business customers and nontechnical goods.
Approved clauses and negotiating limits can be made explicit.
The exception approval step is averaged across cases; routine deals may bypass it.
Signature release uses the same approval recorded in the preceding review step.
The conversation-heavy prior fits; the largest gains concern preparation and paperwork.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates, including access and applicable national consultation.
unknowns: Who can approve discounts, payment concessions, liability clauses, and signature release.
Whether an approved clause library and structured deal terms exist.
Whether {CLM} and {ESIGN} expose usable configuration or interfaces.
Whether credit exposure and margin data are accessible to the representative.
Whether the proposed records would introduce employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which contract fields and clauses can be generated using existing {CLM} configuration?
How accurately does bounded comparison identify material differences in representative historical contracts?
Which national rules affect signature authority and employee consultation?
What GDPR access and retention controls are needed for customer contact and negotiation records?
new_work: Review clause flags and route unfamiliar obligations to legal counsel.
Maintain commercial limits, clause versions, and approval routing.
Resolve differences between approved terms and generated documents.
Check that signature requests use the exact approved version.
Maintain access controls and integration failure alerts.

tasks.short: Translate customer requirements into suitable drawings, estimates, and bids.

steps.what: Read the customer request and extract quantities, dimensions, dates, and requested options.

loop.output: Structured requirements with source references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; show source passages for quantities, dimensions, and deadlines.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per request; ambiguous or missing requirements go to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive as varied prose and documents. Structured forms can replace this loop where customers use them.

steps.what: Clarify intended use, constraints, and priorities with the customer.
Select suitable products and identify departures from standard configurations.
Adapt a standard drawing in the {OTHER} drawing tool to the selected products.
Calculate quantities, prices, freight, lead times, and margin in the estimate workbook.
Assemble the bid with drawings, estimated prices, scope, assumptions, and exclusions.
Review bid completeness and approve commercial exceptions.
Send the approved bid and record its version and follow-up date.

tasks.design: Configure product rules and pricing in {ERP} where supported, and use deterministic generators for estimates, bid templates in {DOCS}, and standard drawings through {OTHER}. A bounded extraction loop converts requests from {EMAIL} into a requirements brief; the representative confirms fit, and {WORKFLOW} releases the exact approved bid and records follow-up in {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrive in mixed formats, while product rules, drawings, prices, and bid documents are maintained separately. Bespoke combinations resist simple templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configurators demonstrate controlled quoting. Faster coding makes template generation and record connections more affordable, with bounded extraction for unstructured requests.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete specifications, unusual combinations, drawing-library maintenance, and reliable delivery commitments. Novel drawings still need a competent person.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's intended use and notice where a plausible configuration fails in practice.

ambition.what: Side-by-side bids for a standard option and a lower-cost alternative

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time clarifying needs and comparing alternatives, with less copying between drawings and estimates. They can explore more options within existing pricing limits; formal approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Check fit and constraints when a requested layout exceeds standard drawing rules.
reach.learn: Dimensional tolerances, installation constraints, and the boundary between illustrative and technical drawings.

reach.task: Convert accepted bid lines into an accurate order.
reach.learn: Item identifiers, option codes, units, delivery commitments, and version matching.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad offers configuration and quoting linked to ERP and CRM records.
The ZARGES vendor case reports quote preparation falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds.
Parametric templates can generate standard drawings; the digest does not establish coverage for bespoke drawings.
Bounded extraction can support varied customer requests when source references and field checks accompany review.

assumptions: Drawings are sales layouts or product illustrations, not engineering certification.
A useful share of bids follows standard product and drawing families.
The scenario includes a workbook joining prices, freight, and margin; some firms already calculate these in {ERP}.
Manager review is averaged across cases and may be limited to exceptions.
Bid release uses the approval recorded in the preceding review step.
The judgement-heavy prior applies to fit and clarification; standard calculations and document assembly have greater rule coverage.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates; creating a missing product-rule library would add substantial work.
unknowns: Share of standard versus bespoke drawings and bids.
Whether product combinations, pricing, freight, and lead-time rules are maintained.
Drawing tool interfaces and template licensing.
Who approves product suitability and commercial exceptions.
Whether the representative can access current stock and margin data.
research_questions: Which product families support deterministic drawing generation?
Can existing {ERP} configuration replace the estimate workbook?
What extraction accuracy is achievable on representative historical requests?
Which fields need explicit customer confirmation before a bid is issued?
What national consultation is required if bid records change employee monitoring?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve ambiguous units or dimensions.
Maintain configuration rules, drawing templates, prices, and freight rates.
Route bespoke drawings and unusual product combinations to specialists.
Check stale availability and delivery assumptions.
Resolve generation failures and retain approved bid versions.

tasks.short: Collect and verify prospective customer credit information for finance review.

steps.what: Confirm the prospective customer's legal identity and check for an existing account.
Request missing business details, financial information, or trade references from the customer.
Retrieve a report from the {OTHER} credit-information service and check internal payment history.
Compare entity details, report dates, references, and payment records; flag conflicting or missing information.
Assemble the evidence, source dates, and unresolved questions into a credit dossier.
Check dossier relevance, forward it to finance, and record the review request.

tasks.design: Configure a credit-information checklist in {CRM} and connect {ERP} with the {OTHER} credit-information service through {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks match legal entities, flag stale or conflicting evidence, and assemble a restricted dossier in {DOCS}; the representative approves its handoff to finance through {WORKFLOW}, with GDPR access and retention controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report access, entity identifiers, and internal payment history were disconnected. Manual collection also obscured which evidence was missing or stale.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured service interfaces and existing record workflows can handle collection. Faster integration development makes a narrow evidence pipeline more affordable; no model is needed for the assumed inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Entity ambiguity, report licensing, missing references, personal data, and deciding what adverse information means. Finance retains credit assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Spot the wrong legal entity, obtain context for conflicting evidence, and ask sensitive questions without damaging the relationship.

ambition.what: Monthly prioritisation of growing accounts needing refreshed credit evidence

tasks.altitude: Routine collection takes less time, leaving more capacity for missing evidence and customer follow-up. No new credit-approval rights are gained; the representative can propose refresh priorities to finance.

reach.task: Complete a verified customer account dossier before account activation.
reach.learn: Legal entity matching, required account fields, evidence provenance, and lawful data handling.

reach.task: Identify opportunities delayed by incomplete credit evidence.
reach.learn: Credit review stages, evidence freshness, and finance escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Structured credit-report retrieval, entity checks, and dossier generation can use deterministic integrations.
GDPR applies where business credit records contain personal data, including contact or sole-trader information.
Evidence collection and credit approval are separate activities; automated collection need not automate the decision.

assumptions: This task ends at evidence handoff; credit approval belongs to finance.
The credit-information service offers licensed structured access.
Missing-data requests use approved fields and templates.
Customer documents outside the structured path remain exceptions handled by a person.
The structured-input prior supports substantial collection automation; identity and evidence relevance still need review.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates, including access and applicable national consultation.
Operating cost depends mainly on credit-report fees and access licensing.
unknowns: Who currently retrieves reports and who owns credit assessment.
Available report licenses, interfaces, and reuse restrictions.
Quality of legal entity identifiers and duplicate account records.
Customer mix, including sole traders and other records containing personal data.
Approved lawful basis, retention period, and finance access permissions.
Whether finance wants periodic refreshes as well as checks on new prospects.
research_questions: Which existing {ERP} or {CRM} configuration can handle the checklist and handoff?
Which report fields can be retrieved and retained under the service license?
Which deterministic checks catch historical entity mismatches and stale reports?
What GDPR controls and national rules apply to the actual customer records?
What employee consultation applies if the workflow introduces seller activity tracking?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous legal entity matches and conflicting reports.
Maintain evidence freshness thresholds and collection checklists.
Monitor failed lookups, report fees, and license restrictions.
Maintain restricted access and delete records according to retention rules.

role.altitude: The representative spends less time collecting records and rebuilding documents, and more time understanding customers, negotiating trade-offs, and improving retail execution. Formal authority changes only through explicit delegation; commercial, signature, retailer, and credit approvals retain their named owners.
reach: Sales manager: prepare margin scenarios and evidence for commercial exceptions.
Order clerk: turn accepted bids and contracts into accurate order instructions.
Sales engineer: recognise when product fit or drawings require specialist review.
Demonstrator and product promoter: connect display plans with effective demonstrations.
New accounts clerk: assemble verified customer information for account setup.
skills_to_grow: Maintain product, price, and template rules.
Verify extracted requirements against their sources.
Match legal entities and assess evidence freshness.
Use GDPR access and retention controls.
Compare display trials with appropriate baselines.
role.ambitious_version: Offer smaller business customers a coordinated service: suitable product alternatives, clear bids, agreed display plans, and timely account setup. Reuse governed records and templates so the representative can expand useful advice while remaining accountable for customer understanding and commercial judgement.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
